title: 有機化学
subtitle: Organic Chemistry
educationalGoal: Organic compounds outnumber inorganic compounds in the world around us. However, elements that compose organic compounds are relatively few and the bonding types are simple. The purpose of this course is to learn the fundamentals of organic chemistry, including the classification, naming, characteristics, and reactions of organic compounds. You will be able to predict the properties of an organic compound from its chemical structure.
advice:
This course will cover:
1. Atomic structure
2. Properties of chemical bonds
3. Acids and bases
4. Functional groups
5. Alkanes and alkyl groups
6. Configuration of ethane
7. Cycloalkanes
8. Naming of alkenes and electronic structures
9. Reactions of organic compounds
10. Polar covalent bonds
11. Additions of HX to alkenes
12. Reactions of alkenes
13. Methods for producing alkenes
14. Conjugated dienes and alkynes
15. Electrophilic aromatic substitutions
16. Consideration of regional issues from the view of organic chemistry.
books:
Textbooks: Fundamentals of Organic Chemistry, Japanese 7th edition [Tokyo kagaku dojin]
Reference books: Unspecified
Reserved books: Unspecified
requiredKnowledge: Organic chemistry is the basis of biotechnology and applied chemistry. You will need the textbook for this course. Chapters 1 to 6 of the textbook are about organic chemistry, chapters 7 to 12 are about organic synthesis, and the subsequent chapters present concepts of analytical chemistry and biochemistry.

activityGoals.body: Describe the structures of atoms and electron configurations.
Explain ionic bonds and covalent bonds.
Describe the structures of methane, ethane, ethylene, and acetylene
Understand the definitions of acid and base.
Understand the structures of functional groups.
Name and describe alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, and aromatic compounds and understand their reactions.
